messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-response path high error rate and backend queue growth observed. paging #incidents. auto-sampled traces show long stalls in kv-cache layer. region: us-west-2. impact: elevated 5xxs for /v1/stream and increased per-tenant token backlog. suggested immediate mitigations: 1) throttle streaming by reducing concurrency and max-frame-size, 2) flip streaming feature flag to fallback-to-polling for hosted API, 3) shift heavy tenants to reserved capacity. paging @sam oncall.
sam: on it. quick question — do we have a single global kill switch for streaming or per-cluster? :thinking_face:
maria: we have both. admin API supports a cluster-level toggle and a global override. cluster toggle is safer to try first (us-west-2 only).
tim: I'm prepping the toggle. canary plan: 5% of traffic -> disable streaming (fall back to non-streaming chunked responses), monitor p50/p95 and 5xx. if stable for 3m, ramp to 100%.
devon: tagging customer impact: two high-usage enterprise tenants show >30% failed streams and partial payloads. whiteboard: reduce streamed frames and bump per-tenant rate limit to avoid retries thrashing the runtime.
emily: do we have status page message ready? if customers see truncated tokens they need guidance — recommend telling them we temporarily suspend streaming while we stabilize and that non-streaming endpoints are available.
sam: agree. can someone craft the status blurb? I'll hold the toggle until message is posted.
maria: status draft:

"We are investigating elevated error rates for streaming responses in US-WEST-2. As a mitigation, we will temporarily redirect streaming requests to non-streaming endpoints while we stabilize throughput. We expect minimal data loss; ongoing updates here."

@emily please shorten and post.
emily: posted on status.redwood.ai - incident label: partial-degradation-streaming-usw2. linked support ticket #INC-2027. :white_check_mark:
tim: executing canary disable (cluster us-west-2) now. command:

```
# admin api example
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/feature-toggle" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"feature":"streaming_responses","scope":"cluster:us-west-2","enabled":false,"note":"incident 2019001234 canary"}'
```

devon: before you flip, make sure streaming cache eviction is at low risk. last time flipping caused KV storms. check `kv.eviction_rate` and `batcher.queue_depth`.
tim: checked metrics: kv.eviction_rate OK, queue_depth trending down already. flipping now.

incident-bot: action: feature-toggle(streaming_responses, cluster:us-west-2) -> success. canary scope: 5% of traffic. timestamp 2019001252.
sam: monitoring. initial look: p95 latency improved from 750ms -> 210ms for canary users, 5xxs down 60% in canary slice.
maria: good signal. start ramping to 25%.
tim: bumping to 25% via same toggle config. timestamp 2019001258.

incident-bot: canary ramp to 25% applied. watch loops, logging enabled for streaming-fallback.
devon: adding temporary rate-limits for free tier to avoid noisy retries: apply policy `rl:global:stream_fallback=50r/m` for the next 30m.
emily: support note posted to affected customer accounts in Intercom; flagged as high-priority.
sam: after 10m of stable metrics, we'll cut 100% for us-west-2 and then start mitigation across other regions if needed.
maria: also start ingress shaping: deprioritize long-held connections >60s to protect latency SLOs.
sam: 10m stable check at 2019001270 — everything green. proceeding to 100% cluster disable now.

tim: toggled cluster us-west-2 to streaming disabled (100%). incident-bot recorded action at 2019001273.

incident-bot: post-action metrics: p95 for non-streaming paths stable at ~230ms, overall 5xxs down 72% vs alert baseline. backlog cleared by ~65% in 7m.
devon: follow-up actions: 1) keep streaming disabled for 30-45m while we increase batcher capacity and review kernel selection for long sequences; 2) prepare rollback plan to re-enable as a canary if queue_depth and eviction_rate are healthy for 10m.
emily: support update sent: "We have temporarily disabled streaming in US-WEST-2 to protect latency. Non-streaming responses remain available. We'll update in 30 minutes or when we have a fix." :email:
sam: handing off to next oncall @devon at 2019001285. I'll stay reachable for the next 15m for context handover.
devon: acknowledged. I'll own the post-mitigation followups and run the capacity bump. if any regressions, I'll page infra.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigation applied (streaming disabled cluster: us-west-2). severity: degraded. responders: sam (oncall), devon (next). link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/2019001234

emily: filing postmortem stub and tagging for root-cause analysis. assigned to @maria and @devon.
sam: thanks team. continuing monitoring. :thumbsup:"
